newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 17.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 17.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open on Thursday as storms ebbed in the Gulf of Mexico, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1500 local/2000 GMT daily meteorological report.
Crude ports Pajaritos opened at 0700 local/1200 GMT after being closed since Saturday afternoon, as wind speeds and waves calmed.
Ciudad del Carmen, Cayo Arcas, Frontera, Veracruz, Nautla, and Salina Cruz were reported closed to smaller fishing and tourism ships.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.

Winds mild at maximum 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per hour), with some clouds and rains over coasts of Sinaloa, Sonora, Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima and Michoacan. Winds reported at between 15 and 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles per hour) in Gulf of Tehuantepec, with waves five to seven feet high.

Mass of cold air in northern region, where winds 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles), with waves four to six feet high. Light rains along Tamaulipas and Veracruz states. Calmer winds along rest of coastline.
Hot and partly cloudy with winds from 20 to 30 km per hour.
